title: Ops Onboarding & SLO Experimentation Toolkit
content:
Purpose: Quick, pragmatic toolkit for onboarding product and platform teams into SLO ownership and running small field experiments that validate stability improvements without full org-wide SLO rollout. This doc is a hands-on sprint kit for a 4-6 week pilot: operational checklists, experiment templates, measurement signals, and an escalation-lite path for early failures.

Context and problem statement:
- We have many service teams with partial telemetry and inconsistent SLO practices. Full SLO adoption is high value but expensive/time-consuming to do everywhere at once.
- We need a low-friction way to: (1) onboard a team to SLO thinking, (2) run targeted experiments that exercise batching/caching/fallback policies, and (3) capture measurable signal changes so Product + Eng can decide on broader rollouts.

Goals for the pilot:
1) Onboard 1 product service and 1 infra service to a reproducible SLO experiment flow within 6 weeks.
2) Demonstrate a clear signal: >=10% p50 latency reduction or >=15% token-cost drop on targeted workload after adopting config change or caching policy, without increasing error rate > 0.1%.
3) Produce a templated package (checklist, dashboards, alert rules) that can be reused by other teams.

Scope boundaries:
- Pilot limited to non-customer-facing infra (infra service) and one mid-volume product route (product service).
- No changes to billing or quota contracts.
- No access to customer PII; synthetic or anonymized traces only.

Roles and responsibilities (light RACI):
- SRE Lead (Aisha) - accountabilities: run coordination meetings, validate experiment safety gating, sign off on rollback plan.
- Product Eng (Jon) - responsible for implementing config changes (e.g., KV cache TTL), adding lightweight metrics.
- Observability (Priya) - responsible for dashboards, query definitions, alert thresholds, and log retention window adjustments for the experiment.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Ops (Marcus) - stakeholder liaison, verifies functional correctness for product behavior.
- Reliability Analyst (Lena) - runs statistical comparisons, writes the final experiment summary.

6-week pilot sprint plan (high level):
Week 0: Prep (2 weeks before run)
- Kickoff: align goals, success metrics, and safety constraints.
- Inventory: identify routes, key latency/cost/error metrics, and existing dashboards.
- Baseline collection: 7-14 days of metrics capture; store snapshot queries.
- Safety review: validate rollback controls and quick-disable flags.

Week 1: Lightweight implementation + feature flags
- Implement changes behind feature flags (e.g., batching policy adjustments, prefix cache enablement, quantization toggle for infra).
- Add metric tags/labels to distinguish experiment traffic.
- Create canary route or low-traffic shard for initial verification.

Week 2: Canary validation (3–5 days)
- Run canary for at least 48 hours, monitor p50/p90/p99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and token cost per request.
- Check functional correctness with smoke test suite provided by product.
- If any safety signals hit threshold, rollback immediately and log incident.

Week 3: Ramp and comparative experiments
- Gradually increase traffic to 10–25% of normal volume for product route; infra can be 25–50% depending on service.
- Start A/B style comparison: control vs. experiment slices, use consistent randomization keys.

Week 4: Measurement and analysis
- Freeze config changes and collect final 7-day measurement window if possible.
- Reliability Analyst runs paired statistical tests on p50 and token-cost per successful request.
- Produce a short decision memo: keep (roll out), iterate (another experiment), or abandon.

Week 5–6: Rollout or rollback + templating
- If metrics pass acceptance criteria and no functional regressions, prepare rollout playbook for wider teams.
- If failed, capture learnings, adjust hypotheses, and propose follow-up experiments.

Safety thresholds (pre-agreed):
- Error rate increase > 0.1% absolute -> immediate rollback.
- P99 tail latency regression > 25% vs baseline -> pause ramp and investigate.
- CPU/GPU sustained >85% for >10min -> throttle ramp and assess autoscale.

Experiment templates (pick one per pilot):
1) Caching experiment (product route):
- Hypothesis: Enabling prefix KV cache with TTL=30s reduces average per-request latency by >=10% on routes with 60% prefix reuse.
- Implementation: Toggle cache flag behind ff, instrument cache-hit metric and per-request token counts.
- Measurement: cache_hit_ratio, p50/p90 latency, successful_request_token_count.
- Safety: fallback to cache-miss behavior if functional mismatch detected.

2) Batching experiment (infra inference endpoint):
- Hypothesis: Increasing batch window to 60ms for low-latency-critical but throughput-sensitive workloads reduces cost per token by >=15% while keeping p99 < 1.5x baseline.
- Implementation: add batching flag, isolate traffic to test shard, measure batch sizes and queue delay histogram.
- Measurement: average_batch_size, queue_wait_ms, p99/p90 latency, cost_per_token.

3) Quantization profile test (infra model variant):
- Hypothesis: Moving to int8 quantized variant reduces GPU memory footprint and token cost with <1% accuracy degradation on small eval prompt set.
- Implementation: deploy quantized variant behind routing policy, route 10% test traffic.
- Measurement: correctness on eval prompts, p50 latency, vram_utilization, inference_cost.

Dashboards & signal definitions (minimum set):
- Baseline dashboard snapshot name: slo-experiment-baseline-<service>-YYYYMMDD (store as saved query).
- Experiment dashboard: experiment-<service>-<id> showing side-by-side control vs experiment: p50/p90/p99, error_rate, success_rate, cost_per_request, resource_utilization, cache_hit_ratio, batch_size_histogram.
- Automated comparison panels: delta_pct for each key metric and a simple green/yellow/red status tile based on thresholds above.

Quick incident playbook (short):
1) Owner notices anomaly -> page SRE Lead.
2) SRE Lead evaluates: runbook quick checks (feature flag status, recent deploys, infra metrics).
3) If threshold breach -> flip feature flag to control state, drain test shard, notify stakeholders, open postmortem ticket.
4) For non-safety anomalies -> slow ramp, add instrumentation, consult Reliability Analyst.

Acceptance criteria for successful pilot:
- One experiment meets the goal (latency or cost improvement) and does not violate safety thresholds for a 7-day stabilized window.
- Templates (checklist, dashboard, alert rule) created and documented in Confluence.
- Two other teams sign up for the templated flow in the next quarter.

Risk matrix (top-level):
- Functional regressions: risk low-medium; mitigations: feature flags, canary route, rapid rollback.
- Measurement noise / false positives: risk medium; mitigations: paired tests, min sample sizes, statistical tests.
- Resource contention: risk medium; mitigations: limit traffic ramp, allocate separate GPU pool for infra experiments if needed.

Deliverables by pilot end:
- Experiment summary memos for product and infra teams.
- Reusable checklist: preflight, canary validation, ramp sheet, rollback steps.
- Saved dashboard queries and alert templates in shared observability folder.
- Short retro notes with 3 concrete follow-ups.

Communication cadence and channels:
- Twice-weekly 30m sync for pilot owners (Mon/Wed) during active weeks.
- Slack channel: #reliability-pilot-ops-<service>-<id> for live updates.
- Decision memo posted to Confluence with action items and owner assignments.

Onboarding checklist (practical):
- [ ] Confirm experiment scope and obtain Product sign-off.
- [ ] Create baseline dashboard and snapshot queries.
- [ ] Implement feature flags and confirm rollback controls.
- [ ] Add experiment labels to telemetry.
- [ ] Run smoke tests on canary shard.
- [ ] Schedule ramp windows and stakeholders oncall.
- [ ] Define success criteria and safety thresholds in writing.

Next steps (to start now):
- Schedule kickoff with selected teams (owner: Aisha) by 2026-03-08.
- Product Eng to nominate product route and provide smoke-test suite by 2026-03-10.
- Observability to prepare baseline saved queries by 2026-03-12.

Notes and open questions (to resolve during kickoff):
- Which persistence of saved queries is acceptable for later audit (retain 90 days vs 365 days)?
- Is a separate GPU pool budgetable for infra experiments if contention appears?
- Should we include customer success in communications for product-visible experiments?

Appendix: short example decision memo template to use after measurement:
- Title: Experiment decision: <service> <experiment-name> <date>
- Summary: 2–3 lines of primary outcome
- Metrics (baseline vs experiment): p50, p90, p99, error_rate, cost_per_request, sample_size
- Safety incidents: yes/no + short description
- Recommendation: roll out / iterate / abandon + next steps + owner

End of doc.
